payload.title: All-Inclusive Greece Wedding Packages Compared
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, who want a Greek wedding without assembling every supplier themselves. They have seen 'all inclusive' on several Greek venue packages across Crete, Rhodes, Corfu, Mykonos, Paros, Santorini and the mainland, and now want to see what each one actually puts inside the package, what is charged on top, and whether an all-inclusive package suits their guest list or whether they should build their own.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can compare the couple's shortlisted all-inclusive Greek packages like for like, with the quote in AUD and inclusions confirmed in writing before they commit.
payload.angle: 'All inclusive' on a Greek venue package means different things from one island to the next. Page-one results either sell a single package or list prices; this guide puts 8 to 10 named Greek venue packages side by side by what each venue states it includes (ceremony type, set-up, coordinator, food and drink, spaces and hours) and what it charges on top or requires (exclusive use, guest rooms and minimum nights, extra hours, outside suppliers, documents). It says plainly what 'all inclusive' usually covers at a Greek venue and what it rarely covers, compares without ranking, and gives a like-for-like quote checklist. No prices, so the comparison stays true when rates change.
must_include: Intro (60 to 120 words): direct answer in the first 100 words (an all-inclusive Greek venue package usually bundles the ceremony set-up, a coordinator, food and drink for set hours in set spaces; exclusive use, guest rooms, extra hours and outside suppliers vary by venue); link /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages and /destination-wedding-packages prominently in the intro, and /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-packages prominently in the Santorini entry or intro.
Exactly 4 Key takeaways, each one sentence, no figures.
What 'all inclusive' means at a Greek venue: what it usually covers and what it rarely covers, only as venues state it.

Comparison table of 8 to 10 named Greek venue packages (columns: venue and island, package, ceremony type, main inclusions, extras charged on top, requirements or minimums with no money), plus a short entry per venue in fresh wording; venue names only where their package is described; compare, never rank; 'charged on top' or 'a fee applies' only where the venue says so.

Island guides linked once each where relevant: /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/corfu-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues.

How to compare two all-inclusive quotes like for like: inclusions in writing, per-guest or fixed (as a question), deposits and cancellation, exclusive use and days, music times, weather plan, step-free access, quote currency; the single body Advisor line sits in the Australian angle section.
When all inclusive suits you and when to build your own: practical trade-offs, no planner or vendor names.

Legal in brief, as at November 2026: one short paragraph, link /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues legal section or the Santorini planning guide; venue paperwork offers only as the venue's own offer, once each; nothing implies the Wedded Advisor handles legal, church or religious paperwork.

Australian angle: one Advisor line from brand-facts.md only (quotes in AUD for Australian couples, inclusions confirmed in writing before the couple commits); deposit and cancellation terms and travel insurance only as questions.
FAQ and close: close invites a Wedded Concierge consultation, one Wedded Advisor as a single point of contact, brand-facts claims only.

Links: /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages, /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-packages, /destination-wedding-packages (all prominent); /destinations/europe/greece; /wonderland-concierge with UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing; /magazine. Anchor text says 'Wedded Concierge', never 'Wonderland Concierge'. Each source linked once.
avoid: Any price, fee, euro or AUD amount, 'from' price, percentage, per-person figure or deposit size anywhere, including table, FAQ, meta and alt text.
'Best', ranking or scoring packages; calling a package all inclusive unless the venue says so.
Research talk ('on its own site', 'in its own words', what we could or could not find); 'often told' more than once; hedge stacking; linking any source more than once.
Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body; Wedded Privileges; transfer offers; 'last dance' or the brand-facts line containing it.
Any implication that the Wedded Advisor handles legal, church or religious paperwork; legal meanings not in an official source.
Planner or other vendor names; venue contact or business details; implied partnerships or preferred rates.
Competitor sites, directories, planner blogs, review sites or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images.
Repeating the Greece packages guide, Santorini packages guide or island venue guides; summarise and link.
Em dashes, US spelling, exclamation marks, clichés, keyword-stuffed headings.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding; unlicensed images (placeholders only).
payload.cannibalisation_check: Highest overlap in the series. /destination-wedding-packages (live, 'All-Inclusive Destination Wedding Packages') owns generic all-inclusive intent; /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages (draft) owns 'greece wedding packages'; /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-packages (draft) owns Santorini package terms; /all-inclusive-wedding-cost and /destination-weddings/all-inclusive-wedding-cost cover cost intent. This page differs as a Greece-only, venue-by-venue inclusions comparison with no prices, and links the first three prominently. SEO to check volume and rankings for 'greece wedding packages all inclusive' and variants; if demand is tiny or merges with the head term, the run report recommends keeping this as a comparison page or folding it into the Greece packages guide.
payload.intro_plan: Open on the reader's problem (several Greek packages all called all inclusive, none alike), give the direct answer in the first 100 words, link the Greece packages guide and /destination-wedding-packages.
key_takeaways_plan: An all-inclusive Greek venue package usually covers the ceremony set-up, a coordinator and food and drink for set hours, and the rest depends on the venue.
Exclusive use, guest rooms, extra hours and outside suppliers are where Greek all-inclusive packages differ most.
Compare two quotes only on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency, with every inclusion in writing.
All inclusive suits couples who want one set of terms, while building your own suits those who want full control of suppliers.
